transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-20 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alice Turner (Redwood AE), Ben Chang (Redwood SE), Liam Park (Redwood SE), Rachel Li (FluxMetrics - Head of ML), Tom Ortega (FluxMetrics - Infra), Priya Nair (FluxMetrics - CTO), Samir Patel (FluxMetrics - ML Eng)

Auto-summary: Quick walkthrough of Optimize quantization profiles. Demo of console showing latency and quality curves for INT8 and FP8, plus fallback rules. Agreed next steps: share benchmarks, schedule POC, security review.

Transcript:
00:00 Alice (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alice, AE on the account, and with me is Ben from the SE team and Liam who owns some of our quantization work. How's everyone?
00:15 Rachel (FluxMetrics): Hi Alice, thanks. We got about 45 mins. We're mainly curious about INT8 and FP8 — our cost curve looks bad with current models and we want to see the quality delta and whether Redwood Optimize can help.
00:30 Ben (Redwood SE): Great. Today's plan: quick context, then a live console demo of quant profiles, show the quality vs latency graphs, and then go over policies (fallbacks, canarying). We'll also surface what we recommend for a POC.
00:45 Priya (FluxMetrics): Perfect. Our constraints: strict latency SLOs (95p < 250ms for short prompts), SOC2 requirements, and we have some sensitive prompts — KMS important.
01:05 Ben: Understood. We support KMS integrations and audit logs; we'll share the security pack after. For latency we can show both hosted and Dedicated numbers; Optimize suggests batch and quant profiles per route.
01:30 Samir (FluxMetrics): Quick question — do you support mixed precision? Like FP8 on some layers, INT8 on others?
01:45 Liam (Redwood SE): Yes — our quant profiles are pretty flexible. Optimize can suggest per-model profiles: full INT8, FP8 (where supported), and hybrid profiles. The console shows quality regressions measured against your eval set.
02:10 Alice: We'll jump to the console. I'm sharing my screen — bear with me if the video quality is meh, sometimes the screen share compresses a bit.
02:30 [screen share start — Redwood Console: Optimize -> Quantization Profiles]
03:00 Ben: Here is the quant profiles dashboard. On the left you see model variants and the profiles we tested. On the right are two key charts: latency (ms per token) and quality delta (ROUGE/accuracy-like metric we compute per eval) vs token cost.
03:35 Rachel: That quality metric — is that from our eval set or a Redwood default?
03:45 Ben: We ran this demo with a synthetic eval for demo purposes; for your POC we'd plug in your 50 prompts and measure exact deltas. The metric is customizable — we normalize across your prompts.
04:05 Ben: Ok show first the baseline FP32 numbers — this is our hosted baseline for the selected model (open-llama-7b-ish, note: model name may be slightly different in transcript). FP32 latency: 240ms 95p for these short prompts, cost X tokens.
04:35 Ben: Now the INT8 profile — you can see a 40-50% latency improvement and approx 45% token compute cost reduction, but quality delta is non-zero for some prompt categories (long-form reasoning suffers slightly).
05:05 Liam: For FP8 (we label it FP8/FORMAT in the console sometimes), the latency improvement is similar to INT8 in some backends but quality often holds better on certain models; it's model- and kernel-dependent. FP8 can be a sweet spot, but it's newer and not all kernels/hardware have identical behavior.
05:40 Rachel: Can you show an example prompt where INT8 regresses?
05:50 [ben navigates to example diffs view]
06:10 Ben: Here — prompt category 'multi-step extraction' — baseline answers vs INT8 vs FP8. INT8 missed a sub-step in 3/50 prompts; FP8 kept it in 48/50. We flag those as potential regressions and Optimize will surface them in the console.
06:40 Tom: How are these measured? Is it exact string match or semantic similarity?
06:50 Ben: We support both. For this demo it's a mixture — a fuzzy token-match metric and a manual review sample. For your POC we recommend a mix of exact checks and human spot-checks for the critical flows.
07:15 Alice: Also important: you can configure automatic fallback policies. If quality metric for a route dips below threshold, the router will route to FP32 or FP8 fallback. You can set thresholds per route.
07:40 Priya: What's the cost delta of enabling a fallback? If we hit fallback frequently, we could lose cost benefit.
07:50 Liam: Right — Optimize provides an expected blended cost estimate based on historical fallback rates. For instance, if INT8 is used 90% and fallback FP32 10%, you'll get a blended token cost. We show that projection in the console.
08:20 Samir: Do you handle prefix/KV cache interactions differently for quantized kernels? We use long chat sessions a lot.
08:35 Ben: Good question. KV cache behavior is mostly runtime invariant, but quantized kernels sometimes change memory layout; our runtime manages KV cache mapping so latency for cached steps stays low. There's occasional micro-regression for certain FP8 paths but Optimizer tests that and flags if cache invalidations cause issues.
09:05 Rachel: Can you run a quick latency comparison table for Dedicated vs Hosted with INT8/FP8?
09:15 [Ben toggles model and infra view]
09:30 Ben: Hosted: FP32 baseline 240ms 95p. INT8 hosted ~130-150ms 95p. FP8 hosted ~140ms 95p but with slightly better quality. Dedicated (reserved GPUs) drops both by 20-30ms on average: INT8 ~110-120ms 95p, FP8 ~115-125ms. These are demo numbers — we'll run your exact workload in the POC and produce CSVs.
10:05 Priya: That's promising. Any known compatibility issues with our NVIDIA A100s?
10:15 Liam: A100s are well-supported. FP8 support depends on runtime and kernels; we have optimized FP8 kernels for Ampere and Hopper variants. If you have older hardware, INT8 is more broadly compatible.
10:40 Tom: Security — SOC2, SSO (SAML), RBAC — does Optimize or Dedicated change audit expectations?
10:50 Alice: We can run Private deployments with customer-managed KMS. For Hosted/Dedicated we provide audit logs and RBAC; for PII-sensitive workloads we often recommend Dedicated with VPC peering and KMS. We'll share the SOC2 pack.
11:20 Rachel: What about drift detection? If quantization causes silent quality drift over time, can Optimize alert?
11:30 Ben: Yes — there's quality monitoring tied to eval sets and canarying. If your metric moves beyond a threshold, Optimize can auto-roll back or create an alert to Slack/email.
11:55 Samir: On the POC, how invasive is the instrumentation? We can't ship production prompts to a vendor.
12:05 Alice: For POC we can run a shadow mode: you send anonymized prompts or a sampled synthetic prompt set we can run in your environment (Dedicated). We still recommend sending a small representative prompt set (50-200 prompts) — ideally anonymized — so Optimize can tune profiles.
12:35 Rachel: Ok we can provide 50 prompts and traffic shape.
12:45 [Ben opens the Optimize recommendations panel and shows suggested profile: Hybrid-FP8-primary with INT8 fallback for one route]
13:10 Ben: Here's a recommended profile per route. You can see expected latency, cost, and projected quality regression probability. For this route (short Q&A) we recommend INT8 primary; for multi-step reasoning we recommend FP8 primary.
13:40 Priya: Can you make those route rules automated? Like route by prompt length or by detected intent?
13:50 Liam: Yes — Smart routing supports policies by route, path, or custom header. You can also route by content hash; for more advanced intent routing we'd recommend a light-weight classifier in front.
14:10 Tom: If we do Dedicated POC, what does infra need to provide?
14:20 Alice: For Dedicated: we typically need three GPUs for initial POC, network peering info if you want VPC, and access for one infra engineer for setup. We manage model deployment and runtime configs.
14:40 [demo continues with console exports and sample CSVs]
15:10 Ben: I'm exporting the benchmark CSV now — will attach to the follow-up. You can see columns: prompt, baseline_score, int8_score, fp8_score, latency_fp32, latency_int8, latency_fp8.
15:35 Rachel: Nice. A couple of nitty-gritty items: how do you handle model version pinning with quant profiles? If we upgrade model, will profiles break?
15:50 Liam: Profiles are tied to model versions. When you upgrade we surface a compatibility check and recommend new profiles; Optimize can run a preflight on the new version. We also support canary rollouts to mitigate breakage.
16:15 Samir: Any gotchas with tokenizer differences and quantization?
16:25 Ben: Tokenizer differences are independent but we normalize token counts in the console; the bigger risk is semantics changing across model versions, which is why we recommend eval-driven gating.
16:45 Priya: What about latency tail under load? If we have bursts, does batching interfere with SLOs?
16:55 Ben: Optimize suggests batching settings per route; for SLO-sensitive routes we recommend lower batching and dedicated capacity. We also have burst capacity options in Dedicated.
17:20 Rachel: Are there any cases where FP8 is strictly worse than INT8?
17:30 Liam: On some older kernel stacks FP8 had higher variance and occasionally worse tail latency. Generally FP8 gives better quality for similar latency, but it depends on the backend. We show the backend-specific tradeoffs in the console.
18:00 Tom: Can you show the fallback config UI?
18:10 [Ben demos fallback UI: set threshold, fallback target, percent to sample, notify hooks]
18:35 Ben: You can set automatic rollback, or sample 1% of traffic to baseline for monitoring. You can also hook to Slack, Sentry, or a webhook.
19:00 Priya: Great. Anything about billing? If we have blended fallback rates, do we bill for actual tokens used?
19:10 Alice: Yes, billed on actual tokens processed and model variant used. The console's cost projection helps estimate monthly spend given expected fallback rates.
19:35 Rachel: One more: do you have any customer stories or benchmarks on similar workloads?
19:45 Alice: We ran a POC with a GenAI startup last quarter — they achieved ~0.5x token-cost with INT8 and got FP8 for the hardest routes, with automated fallback catching 98% of regressions. We'll attach that case study.
20:10 [discussion shifts to logistics and next steps]
20:30 Alice: Quick recap: we'll share the exported CSVs and the quantization spreadsheet, Ben will prepare the recommended config and fallback policy, and we'll plan Dedicated POC. Any other asks?
20:45 Rachel: Please include the SOC2 and KMS integration notes. Also include data retention options.
20:55 Alice: Noted. We'll send the pack by Friday.
21:10 Tom: For POC scheduling, prefer week of 5/26.
21:20 Alice: We'll aim for that.
21:30 Priya: Thanks — this was helpful.
21:40 Alice: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the artifacts and a proposed POC plan.
21:50 [call ends]
